newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Hong Kong democratic head warns of confidence fall.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong democratic head warns of confidence fall.

text.p: The chairman of Hong Kong's Democratic Party, Martin Lee, said on Thursday the appointment of a non-elected legislature by China in Hong Kong threatened confidence in the territory's business community.
"The current confidence could be very short-lived...the market is really too hot," Lee told a news conference in Stockholm at the end of a 10-city tour of Europe.
Lee said an appointed legislature went against provisions of the 1984 Sino-British agreement that laid down the terms for Britain to hand back Hong Kong to China on July 1, 1997.

He said his Democratic Party, the largest party in Hong Kong, supported the return of the territory to China but was fiercely opposed to the appointed legislature that had the power to amend laws and curtail people's freedom.
"Freedoms will no longer be protected by law," Lee said.
"Business people all cherish their freedom more than anything else. I know some business people who have already left Hong Kong because of the prospect of losing their freedom," he said.
